summary: Arranges multiple TOP inputs or referenced TOP paths into rows, columns, or grids, with fit controls for how each image occupies its cell.

key_params.name: top
key_params.note: Additional TOP path list included before wired inputs

key_params.name: scaleres
key_params.note: Scale output resolution by row/column layout when using input resolution

key_params.name: align
key_params.note: none, horizlr, horizrl, verttb, vertbt, gridrows, or gridcols

key_params.name: fit
key_params.note: fill, fithorz, fitvert, fitbest, fitoutside, or nativeres cell fitting

key_params.name: numrows
key_params.note: Number of rows for the selected row layout

key_params.name: numcols
key_params.note: Number of columns for the selected column layout

key_params.name: bcolor
key_params.note: Border color components bcolorr, bcolorg, bcolorb, bcolora

key_params.name: borders
key_params.note: Per-side border widths bordersl, bordersr, bordersb, borderst

key_params.name: bgcolor
key_params.note: Background fill color for uncovered area

key_params.name: compover
key_params.note: Composite over background where alpha is less than one

common_gotchas: TOP paths listed in the top parameter appear before wired inputs when both are used.
Scale Resolution can produce very large textures when many high-resolution inputs are laid out.
Fit Outside and Native Resolution can crop or expose cell background depending on cell size.
rowlayout and collayout use compact ids, and collayout is not spelled columnlayout.
legacyxform changes transform matrix behavior and can shift existing layouts.
key_concepts: Positions multiple input TOPs into rows, columns, or grids with equal output cell allocation.
TOP paths in the top parameter are placed before wired inputs when both input styles are used.
Scale Resolution can enlarge the output by row and column count when output resolution uses the input.
Fit controls how each image is scaled or cropped inside its allotted cell.
Transform-page controls apply per-input 2D transforms after layout cell assignment.
Border and background controls fill the non-image area around laid-out inputs.
